jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Accounts & Automation
jobs.jd_full:
Overview of the Role

We’re on a mission to modernize insurance - making it simpler, more accessible, and customer-first. The insurance industry is a $1T market that’s remained largely untouched by the digital revolution, and PolicyMe is here to change that. As a remote-first, Toronto-based startup with big ambitions, we’re looking for a product leader to help us build the future of insurance in Canada - and beyond.

We are now seeking a Principal Product Manager to join our Accounts & Automation team within our product organization. This role will own several areas of scope, including:

  • Defining the strategy and roadmap to make us the go-to provider for all of our customers’ personal insurance needs, including the platform-wide programs and features that drive multi-product adoption
  • Building trust digitally across the products we offer, so customers feel similar levels of confidence and reassurance as they would get when they speak with one our licensed advisors
  • Evolving our accounts product and internal tools to streamline operations and deliver a seamless customer experience end to end.

This is a highly strategic and hands-on leadership role that blends product vision, analytical thinking, structured execution, and cross-functional leadership. You will be responsible for shaping long-term product direction while also driving day-to-day execution across multiple complex initiatives. Reporting to the VP of Product, you will work closely with leaders across Engineering, Design, Growth, Operations, Customer Success, and Data to build products that create exceptional customer outcomes and drive meaningful business impact.

What you'll be doing

Define & Own the Product Vision

  • Evolve our product strategy to improve customer delight, retention, referral growth, operational efficiency, and cross-product adoption.
  • Develop a compelling long-term vision for how to make insurance simple for Canadians, from how customers discover new products of ours to how they manage it post-sale.
  • Build and champion a roadmap that balances innovation, operational excellence, and long-term scalability.
  • Develop a deep understanding of customer and operational pain points, using those insights to shape strategy and prioritization.
  • Establish clear OKRs and success metrics that align teams around measurable business and customer outcomes.

Solve Ambiguous Problems

  • Take open-ended, unstructured problems and break them down into clear opportunities, strategic priorities, and executable plans.
  • Bring creative, first-principles thinking to solve complex challenges that have not been solved before in the Canadian insurance market.
  • Balance customer needs, technical constraints, operational realities, and business priorities when making product decisions.
  • Lead through ambiguity and create clarity for teams and stakeholders across the organization.

Drive End-to-end Execution and Delivery

  • Lead the product team through the full product lifecycle: problem definition, discovery, solution design, scoping, execution, launch, and iteration.
  • While you’ll shape the strategic direction, you’re also highly execution-oriented and willing to dive into the details when needed.
  • Ensure we build the right things, the right way, at the right time by balancing short-term wins with long-term platform investments.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Design and Engineering to build best-in-class customer and internal product experiences.
  • Write clear, actionable product specifications that connect business goals, customer needs, operational requirements, and technical constraints.
  • Coordinate closely with Growth, Customer Success, Operations, and other stakeholders to ensure launches are operationally ready and well-supported.
  • Drive alignment across teams and act as the connective tissue between stakeholders with competing priorities.

Measurement, Experimentation and Iteration

  • Define success metrics and measurement frameworks for all major initiatives, including customer engagement, funnel conversion, retention, operational efficiency, and long-term customer value.
  • Design and run experiments to validate hypotheses, de-risk larger investments, and accelerate learning.
  • Partner closely with Data to build dashboards, analyze product performance, and translate insights into actionable next steps - including when to pivot, double down, or sunset initiatives.
  • Use data, customer insights, and business context to continuously refine strategy and prioritization.

What we are looking for

  • 8+ years of product management experience, including experience owning and scaling customer-facing digital products in high-growth environments.
  • Strong track record of leading complex cross-functional initiatives and delivering measurable business and customer outcomes.
  • Experience building both customer-facing D2C products and operational/internal tooling products.
  • Experience building prototypes with AI.
  • Experience scaling products and product practices within high-growth startups or fast-moving technology organizations.
  • Proven ability to define and communicate a compelling product vision that aligns teams and stakeholders around long-term outcomes.
  • Strong business acumen with a deep understanding of how product decisions impact revenue, operations, customer success, retention, and compliance.
  • Exceptional ability to structure ambiguous problems and turn them into clear, actionable plans.
  • Strong operational discipline with the ability to manage competing priorities, maintain momentum, and consistently close loops with stakeholders.
  • Excellent collaboration and stakeholder management skills with high emotional intelligence and a transparent leadership style.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills - able to tailor messaging effectively across executives, engineers, designers, marketers, and operational stakeholders.
  • Comfortable leading initiatives with many moving parts and driving alignment across multiple teams.
  • Strong sense of prioritization and ability to define MVP scope while balancing speed, quality, and long-term scalability.
  • Highly analytical and data-driven, with comfort working with product data, defining metrics, building measurement frameworks, and conducting analyses to inform decisions.

Why join us

  • Generous PTO - 20 vacation days
  • A comprehensive benefits plan with premiums paid in full by PolicyMe
  • Investment in your professional development, including an L&D budget, AI tooling budget, performance reviews twice a year and ongoing feedback to ensure you reach your highest potential
  • An extremely high performing, low-ego, remote-first team that is truly disrupting an old industry
  • Option to work from home or our Toronto-based office (bonus: we cover the costs to bring all our employees in-person twice a year for experiential socials!)
  • Access to stock options based on performance

Compensation

Additional Information

About PolicyMe:

At PolicyMe, we are Canada’s leading digital insurance solution, offering straightforward and affordable financial protection for families from coast to coast. Our product suite includes Life Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, and Health & Dental Insurance, all tailored to Canadians' evolving needs. We also offer B2B2C solutions, partnering with organizations to provide seamless digital insurance options. Founded by a team of insurance experts and technology entrepreneurs, PolicyMe is committed to making insurance simpler and more accessible. Since our launch in 2018, we have grown exponentially, selling over $10 billion in insurance coverage to Canadians.

We are proud of the team we’ve built and are excited for those that are yet to join us. We operate with a remote-first culture, attracting top talent from across Canada. If you’re looking for a fast-paced, collaborative environment, working alongside incredibly ambitious yet humble humans, we may be the right place for you! To learn more, visit www.policyme.com.

jobs.title: Director, AI Center of Excellence
jobs.jd_full:
At Instructure, we believe in the power of people to grow and succeed throughout their lives. Our goal is to amplify that power by creating intuitive products that simplify learning and personal development, facilitate meaningful relationships, and inspire people to go further in their education and careers.
We do this by giving smart, creative, passionate people opportunities to create awesome. And that's where you come in:

About the role.

We're standing up an AI Center of Excellence, and we're looking for a Director, AI Transformation to lead it. You'll own the system that makes Instructure an AI-native company: shared infrastructure, governance, a cross-functional roadmap, and a clear, honest read on impact. You'll partner with leaders in every function to turn AI from scattered pilots into a capability that gets sharper every quarter. This role reports to the SVP, Data.

Our mission for this team is simple: make Instructure the most operationally capable AI-native company in education — turning every function and team into a system that gets smarter and faster every quarter.

What you will be doing.

  • Build the foundation. Stand up and run the shared AI infrastructure — integrations, data boundaries, the approved-model registry, and a standard AI stack with single sign-on and data-loss prevention that every function can build on.

  • Set the guardrails. Charter and run the governance council, and put in place the security, privacy, approval, and quality monitoring that let teams move fast without creating risk.

  • Own the roadmap. Set AI COE priorities in collaboration with other departments

  • Prove the impact. Define the standard metrics for cost, throughput, and quality, and report progress through the AI efficiency scorecard.

  • Build capability. Create centralized training libraries and enablement programs along with HR team, and build the place where teams share what works so the whole company benefits.

  • Lead the operating model. Run a centralized-expertise, decentralized-execution model where the Center of Excellence owns the system, functions own the outcomes

  • Build and grow the team. Hire, coach, and develop the Center of Excellence team, including forward-deployed AI engineers, admins etc

What you need to know and have.

  • 12 or more years of experience in technology, data, or product roles, including 5 or more years leading teams, with a track record of delivering measurable operational impact at scale — not just pilots.

  • 2 or more years working directly with AI or machine-learning systems, including hands-on familiarity with modern AI tooling, agentic systems, and large language models.

  • Deep understanding of the infrastructure, data, and security that production AI requires, including model registries, integrations, single sign-on, and data-loss prevention.

  • Strong governance instincts. You know how to set guardrails for security, privacy, and quality that speed teams up rather than slow them down.

  • Proven ability to influence across an organization, from individual contributors to executives, and to build coalitions in a decentralized operating model.

  • A bias for clear metrics and honest reporting. You measure what matters and you tell the truth about progress.

  • Experience building enablement and training programs that change how people actually work.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex technical topics clear to non-technical audiences.

  • A bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, data, business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. An advanced degree is a plus.

jobs.title: Payments GTM (Go-to-Market) Operations and Strategy Lead
jobs.jd_full:
Please note the internal job title is: Principal Payments GTM Operations and Strategy

Want to build the go-to-market engine for a fast growing payments business?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Payments GTM Operations and Strategy Lead to be part of our Fintech department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.

The team:

We’re building the financial backbone for field service businesses. Our Fintech team is one of the most strategically important and fastest growing parts of Jobber. We help businesses get paid, access capital, understand their financial health, and ultimately stay in business longer.

The future of financial services is embedded, and we’re still early. Small businesses increasingly rely on vertical SaaS platforms like Jobber not just to run their operations, but to manage their money. Payments is the foundation of everything we do in Fintech, and how we go to market with our Get Paid products (invoicing, payments, instant payouts, etc) is the single biggest lever we have to grow the business.

This role will own how Jobber’s payments business grows. Think of this as running the commercial side of a payments business inside a SaaS company.

The role:

Reporting into the VP & GM, Payments and Fintech you will establish Payments GTM Operations as a new function at Jobber. You will bring together every team that touches payments go-to-market (Marketing, Sales, Account Management, Customer Support, Risk, Operations, Analytics, Product Development) and build the programs, processes, and measurement that turn these teams into a coordinated growth engine.

The job has two objectives: help more customers discover and get value from Jobber’s payments products, and accelerate revenue growth for the business.

Day to day, the Payments GTM Operations and Strategy Lead will identify opportunities, design programs, and run experiments to drive adoption and usage of Jobber’s payments products. This will include:

  • Mapping and rebuilding the end-to-end customer journey for payments, from first touch through activation and ongoing usage, working closely with cross-functional partners. This includes identifying where customer-facing teams (sales, post-sales, support) can change their motions to drive better outcomes.

  • Experimenting with a range of actions (e.g. incentives) to drive payments adoption and usage, rapidly iterating based on results.

  • Defining the metrics that matter for payments GTM and holding yourself (and cross-functional partners) accountable to them.

  • Building deep working relationships across GTM teams, Product, RevOps, Analytics, etc. You are the connective tissue between these teams on payments GTM.

  • Using data and qualitative insights to find opportunities, size them, run experiments, and measure results.

  • Staying close to what other vertical SaaS and embedded payments players are doing. Knowing where Jobber can differentiate.

To be successful, you should have:

  • Operating and strategy experience, ideally a mix of both:

    • Operating experience: you have experience identifying opportunities, mobilizing teams, and driving measurable results. Could be Revenue Operations, GTM Operations, Strategy & Operations, Product Commercialization, or a GM/Founder role, ideally at a scaling SaaS or Fintech company.

    • Strategy experience (valued): you have been a strategic partner to senior leaders, making data-driven recommendations. Examples could be Management Consulting, VC, or Strategy & Operations.

  • Deep understanding of payments and financial services business models, metrics, and growth strategies is desirable, particularly financial services for small businesses.

  • Strong data instincts. You use analytics to measure impact, make decisions, and optimize performance. You are not just comfortable with data, you reach for it first.

  • Experience using languages such as SQL to manipulate large data sets is a plus, but not required.

  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to work across GTM teams, Product, Executive Leadership, etc. You translate data into stories and strategies into action plans.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and implement scalable operational processes that enhance efficiency and ultimately drive growth.

  • Passion for helping small businesses succeed through innovative financial solutions.

  • A curious mind and a growth mindset. You are a scrappy learner who can quickly become an expert and build new capabilities.

  • A proactive drive to solve problems. You are capable of bringing structure to ambiguous problems, corralling resources, and delivering results.

  • A preference for working in an ambiguous and fast-paced environment. We’re growing fast and things are changing every day.

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect from time to time. This role is open to candidates anywhere in Canada. Employees who live in one of our hub cities - Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo will participate in their department's in-office schedule, while employees outside our hub cities will work remotely.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $151,200 a midpoint of $177,900 and a maximum salary of $204,500 designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

  • A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

  • A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

  • A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

  • To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.

A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.jd_full:
About Surefire Cyber

Surefire Cyber is redefining the incident response model by delivering a swifter, stronger response to cyber incidents such as ransomware, email compromise, malware, data theft, and other threats. Our client-centric approach reduces stress and provides clients the confidence needed to prepare, respond, and recover from cyber incidents – and fortify their cyber resilience after an event.

Surefire Cyber’s approach and delivery are designed by industry veterans who have worked shoulder-to ­shoulder with law firms, insurance carriers, brokers, law enforcement, and impacted organizations in responding to cyber incidents. We are marshaling this experience to address the industry’s persistent challenges of efficiency, predictability, and transparency.

Job Title: Project Manager

Location: Remote (USA)

Role: Full time / Exempt

What Makes You Stand Out

You are an incredibly motivated and driven Project Manager with foundational knowledge and experience in cybersecurity. You enjoy creating structures from disorganization and composing documentation that can be easily accessed and shared with team members.

You have a passion for business process improvements and participating in change management activities that drive efficiencies and deliver swifter first-class results. As a client-facing professional, you serve as a reliable support system to clients and team members to ensure that all action items are followed through on and exceed desired expectations.

How You’ll Make An Impact

You will play a key role in streamlining efficiencies across the Surefire suite of service offerings, ensuring seamless collaboration and alignment. This position is well-suited for someone with a foundational background in cyber incident response management, enabling them to effectively oversee and drive complex cybersecurity projects within our organization.

At times, the Project Manager will represent Surefire Cyber as consulting resource and interact with team members from our DFIR (Digital Forensic and Incident Response) and Advisory teams to ensure engagements are running smoothly and appropriate after-action items are completed in a timely manner.

Your Role In Action

  • Work closely with and seek guidance from the Director of Customer Success and fellow Project Managers as needed to ensure project roadmaps and initiatives are properly prioritized and delivered upon for Surefire Cyber.
  • Build professional relationships and communicate effectively with internal stakeholders and clients to develop and align a first-class strategy with their overall business and incident response objectives.
  • Participate in project meetings, providing input and feedback on project execution and continuous improvement efforts.
  • Manage cyber incident response projects from initiation to completion, ensuring that projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
  • Facilitate and support project plans, including incident response strategies, incident handling procedures, stakeholder communication plans, and resource allocation, in collaboration with engagement leads, consultants, engineers, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Monitor engagement plans, including goals, deliverables, milestones, and resource allocation, in collaboration with Engagement Leads and DFIR consultant team members.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including IT, legal, HR (Human Resources), and external clients and vendors, to ensure effective incident response execution and communication.
  • Manage project risks, issues, and dependencies, and develop mitigation strategies to ensure effective incident response on active engagements.
  • Assist with post-incident reviews and lessons learned sessions to identify areas for improvement and implement corrective actions for future incident response engagements.
  • Learn and stay up to date with the latest cyber threats, attack techniques, incident response technologies, and best practices, and apply them to project management methodologies.
  • Contribute to incident response teams, establishing clear roles and responsibilities, and fostering a collaborative and results-driven work environment.
  • Ensure compliance with incident response frameworks, regulations, and industry standards throughout the engagement lifecycle.
  • Creates, manages, and distributes project artifacts like Statements of Work (SOW) and budget updates.
  • Lead and manage stakeholders to deliver projects that span across one or more business units.
  • Contributes to establishing practices, templates, policies, and tools to expand and mature capabilities within Incident response.
  • Provide after-hours (on-call/weekend rotational) support as required to address critical incidents and maintain continuous coverage.

jobs.title: Head of Partner Programs, Strategy and Operations
jobs.jd_full:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world’s largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

As the Head of Partner Operations, you will build and own the operating system that allows Apollo’s Partnerships business to scale. Sitting within Revenue Operations, you will be the connective tissue between partner strategy and the company-wide systems, data, processes, and commercial infrastructure that make partner motions work.

This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Systems, Data, Finance, Legal. Partner Managers own relationships and execution; you own the operational infrastructure underneath them and you’ll help co-author our partner strategy. You’ll establish the metrics and reporting that leadership uses to understand partner performance, architect the processes and systems that support different partner motions, and ensure the commercial mechanics behind those motions work reliably.

You’ll operate across Apollo’s technology, agency, integration, and strategic partner ecosystem. The goal isn’t simply to make today’s processes run better. It’s to build a scalable Partner Operations function that can absorb new partner motions, eliminate operational friction, and give the business a clear understanding of where partnerships are creating revenue and where the model needs to evolve.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to build a function, not inherit a playbook.

Partnerships is becoming an increasingly important part of Apollo’s revenue ecosystem, but partner motions create a unique operational challenge: the work crosses organizational boundaries, the data often lives across multiple systems, and the right operating model changes as the business learns.

The Head of Partner Operations will be responsible for turning that complexity into leverage. You’ll help define how Apollo measures partner impact, how partner motions are structured, how systems support them, and how the company can scale partner revenue without scaling operational overhead at the same rate.

The strongest person in this role will leave the Partnerships organization with something substantially better than they found it: a clear operating model, trusted data, scalable systems, reliable commercial mechanics, and a set of partner motions that can evolve without rebuilding the infrastructure from scratch.

What You’ll Do

Key Outcomes: Success in this role will be measured by your ability to:

  • Build the operating system for Partnerships. Establish the processes, systems, data model, and governance that allow Partnerships to operate as a measurable, scalable revenue channel. Define clear ownership across Partner Managers, RevOps, Systems, Data, Finance, Legal, and other stakeholders, and create the operating cadence that keeps the machine running.

  • Architect partner motions and commercial models. Partner with the VP of Partnerships and RevOps to design how different partner motions should work end-to-end, from acquisition and qualification through onboarding, activation, revenue generation, expansion, and renewal. Translate strategy into concrete operating models, including workflows, incentives, tiering, deal mechanics, attribution, systems requirements, and measurement.

  • Create a trusted measurement layer for the partner business. Own the reporting infrastructure that gives leadership visibility into partner-driven performance. Establish the operating definitions, instrumentation, dashboards, and recurring reporting for metrics such as the agency funnel, integration adoption, Partner-Involved ARR, sourced/influenced/managed attribution, and partner cohort NRR. Partner with RevOps, Finance and Analytics, while owning the operationalization and ongoing reliability of the resulting metrics.

  • Turn partner data into a decision-making system. Build the mechanisms that allow Partnerships and company leadership to understand which partners, motions, and investments are driving outcomes. Identify gaps in data quality and attribution, establish clear data ownership, and drive remediation upstream. Help drive decisions about where to invest, what to scale, and what to change.

  • Own the partner systems architecture in partnership with Systems. Translate partnership requirements into a coherent systems roadmap spanning Salesforce, PartnerStack, Crossbeam, Apollo, and other connected tooling. Work with Systems and Data Engineering to ensure partner data is captured correctly, flows between systems, and remains usable for reporting and automation. You won’t be the administrator for every system; you’ll own the requirements, architecture, prioritization, and operating model that make those systems work together.

  • Drive cross-functional initiatives from ambiguity to execution. Partnerships will generate problems that don’t fit neatly inside one team’s ownership. You’ll take ambiguous business needs, turn them into structured requirements, identify the right owners, and drive execution. You are accountable for getting the operating model to a working state even when you don’t directly own every component.

  • Continuously improve the economics and efficiency of the partner motion, but not at the expense of growth. Use operational data to identify friction, leakage, and unnecessary manual work across the partner lifecycle. Develop the business case for process changes, automation, or new tooling, and measure whether those investments actually improve partner productivity, revenue contribution, data quality, or operating leverage.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Business Operations, Partner Operations, Strategy & Operations, or a related function, with experience operating in a B2B SaaS environment and working across multiple GTM functions. Must have direct experience in Partnerships within this.

  • Experience building an operating function from the ground up. You’ve created processes, systems, reporting, and governance where there wasn’t previously a mature operating model, and you know how to balance getting today’s work done with building what will replace it.

  • Strong understanding of partnerships and partner-led motions. You understand the operational mechanics behind agencies, technology/integration partners, channel programs, strategic partnerships, or similar ecosystems. You understand how partner economics, attribution, incentives, deal registration, and partner lifecycle management work.

  • A systems thinker with a builder’s bias. You naturally look for the underlying system behind a recurring problem. Rather than building another workaround, you ask what process, data model, workflow, or automation would prevent the problem from happening again.

  • Strong analytical instincts. You’re comfortable working with funnel, pipeline, revenue, cohort, and attribution data and can move between executive-level business questions and the underlying data required to answer them. You know how to distinguish a measurement problem from a business problem.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership without relying on formal authority. You can align multiple XFN Stakeholders around a shared operating model, make tradeoffs explicit, and drive work to completion even when the underlying components are owned by different teams.

  • Strategic and operational range. You can participate in a conversation about the future of Apollo’s partner strategy in the morning and then get into the details of an attribution definition, Salesforce workflow, or revenue-share process in the afternoon.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and evolving requirements. Partner motions are still being built. You should be comfortable creating structure where there isn’t much, making decisions with incomplete information, and iterating quickly as the business learns.

  • Strong written and verbal communicator. You can write a crisp operating proposal, explain a complex systems dependency to an executive, turn an ambiguous request into requirements for Engineering, and create documentation that a broader team can actually use.

  • High ownership and strong judgment. You know which problems require a durable solution, which can be handled pragmatically, and when to pull in the right functional owner. You optimize for the health of the overall revenue system rather than protecting functional boundaries.

AI Fluency & Tooling

Apollo operates at the intersection of AI and go-to-market, and our Revenue Operations organization is expected to lead from the front. This role requires genuine fluency in leveraging AI as part of how you operate and build.

Using LLMs as an active operating partner. Whether you’re analyzing partner performance, developing SQL, drafting requirements, documenting processes, investigating data quality issues, or preparing an executive recommendation, you should be reaching for AI tools wherever they can materially accelerate your work.

Designing partner operations for an AI-native environment. Think beyond dashboards and workflows toward how structured partner data, documentation, and operating context can be made accessible to AI agents and internal tools. Using AI to increase operating leverage. The expectation is that a single operator can accomplish substantially more by combining strong judgment with AI-assisted analysis, development, automation, and documentation.

Staying ahead of the tooling curve. The AI tooling landscape is moving quickly. We’re looking for someone who experiments, learns independently, shares what works, and continuously looks for ways to replace manual operational work with better systems.

Knowing where AI should and shouldn’t be trusted. AI can accelerate analysis and execution, but it can also introduce hallucinations, incorrect assumptions, and false confidence. You should have strong enough operational and analytical judgment to validate AI-generated outputs and know when first-principles analysis is required.

About Hello Heart:

Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.

We’re an AI company focused exclusively on heart health, building a platform that predicts and prevents cardiac events before they happen—identifying risk up to 10 days in advance versus 10 years in traditional clinical models.

This is already working at scale. Hello Heart has been shown to reduce inpatient hospital days by 47% and deliver ~$1,800 in annual savings per member. Hello Heart is the cardiac prevention partner to over 80% of large U.S. health plans and serves hundreds of public and private employers.

We’re defining how the #1 cause of death—heart disease—is managed in the AI era. Join us.

About the Role

Hello Heart is seeking a Senior Director, GTM Strategy & Operations to help scale how we bring major roadmap investments, new products, new market opportunities, and strategic growth initiatives to life. This role sits at the center of Client Strategy & Growth, Client Experience, Product, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal, Enablement, and our Product & Engineering teams in Tel Aviv. The ideal candidate is a highly strategic yet hands-on operator who can translate ambitious ideas into executable plans, drive alignment across executive stakeholders, and ensure Hello Heart’s most important initiatives successfully move from concept to commercialization.

This is not a traditional project management role. We are looking for an enterprise problem solver and business athlete who thrives in ambiguity, influences without authority, and can partner effectively with senior leaders to turn strategy into measurable business outcomes. Success in this role requires equal parts strategic thinking, commercial judgment, operational excellence, cross-functional leadership, and the ability to leverage AI to improve execution, accelerate decision-making, and increase organizational efficiency. This individual will help shape how Hello Heart launches new capabilities, evolves go-to-market motions, scales commercialization practices, and executes high-impact strategic initiatives across the company.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the company’s biggest new product launches and growth projects.
  • Turn big ideas and leadership goals into clear, step-by-step plans.
  • Work closely with teams across the company, including teams in Tel Aviv, to make sure everyone is ready for new launches.
  • Help leaders make smart decisions by pointing out risks and choices.
  • Fix problems and remove roadblocks to keep projects moving forward.
  • Create simple guides and rules so the company can launch new products smoothly every time.
  • Use AI tools to work faster, save time, and help the team make better decisions.
  • Provide executive leadership with clear, actionable reports to facilitate precise decision-making.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in business, consulting, or healthcare technology.
  • Proven success leading projects at scale with many different teams and leaders.
  • Experience bringing new products or services to market.
  • Great problem-solving skills and the ability to find smart solutions to tough business issues.
  • Ability to build trust with leadership and help drive consensus on major decisions.
  • Strong understanding of how business choices affect customers and company success.
  • Master at staying organized and keeping projects moving even when things are ambiguous and changing fast.
  • Excellent communication skills to explain complicated ideas simply.
  • Experience working with startup companies and international teams, like developers in Tel Aviv.
  • Skilled at using AI tools to get work done faster and smarter.
  • Experience in digital healthcare, health insurance, or consulting is highly desired.
  • Having an MBA or a similar advanced business degree is advantageous but not required.
  • Ability to travel 30-35% of the time
